s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute left leg pain and weakness with systemic inflammation
salient_findings: Increasing left leg pain and weakness over one week
Bilateral iliacus and iliopsoas muscle oedema with enhancement on MRI
key_facts: One week of increasing left leg pain and weakness
Anorexia and 12% body-weight loss over six months
Low blood pressure responsive to IV fluids
Neurologic examination showed 4/5 strength in left hip and knee flexors and extensors
MRI of the lumbar spine showed mild foraminal narrowing at L5–S1 but no central canal stenosis or abscess
Left hip ultrasound revealed a small anterior joint effusion
MRI of the hip and pelvis demonstrated bilateral iliacus and iliopsoas muscle oedema with enhancement

raw.syndrome_frame: Subacute left leg pain and weakness with systemic inflammation
salient_findings: Increasing left leg pain and weakness over one week
Bilateral iliacus and iliopsoas muscle oedema with enhancement on MRI
key_facts: One week of increasing left leg pain and weakness
Anorexia and 12% body-weight loss over six months
Low blood pressure responsive to IV fluids
Neurologic examination showed 4/5 strength in left hip and knee flexors and extensors
MRI of the lumbar spine showed mild foraminal narrowing at L5–S1 but no central canal stenosis or abscess

differentials: Psoas syndrome due to retroperitoneal fibrosis
Tumor necrosis factor receptor-associated periodic syndrome
per_call: Psoas syndrome due to retroperitoneal fibrosis
Tumor necrosis factor receptor-associated periodic syndrome

shortlist.label: Psoas abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated inflammatory markers and muscle oedema with enhancement on MRI

shortlist.label: Polymyalgia rheumatica
shortlist.why_kept: Subacute onset of leg pain and weakness with systemic inflammation

shortlist.label: Pyomyositis
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral iliacus and iliopsoas muscle oedema with enhancement on MRI

shortlist.label: Iliopsoas bursitis
shortlist.why_kept: Small anterior joint effusion on left hip ultrasound and muscle oedema on MRI

shortlist.label: Giant cell arteritis
shortlist.why_kept: Systemic inflammation and elevated inflammatory markers in an elderly patient

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of increasing left leg pain and weakness, impaired mobility, and elevated inflammatory markers, combined with the MRI findings of bilateral iliacus and iliopsoas muscle oedema with enhancement, is most consistent with pyomyositis, a bacterial infection of the skeletal muscle.

rejected.label: Psoas abscess
rejected.why: The MRI of the lumbar spine and hip did not show an abscess in the psoas muscle

rejected.label: Polymyalgia rheumatica
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and laboratory results do not meet the typical criteria for polymyalgia rheumatica, which includes shoulder and hip girdle pain and stiffness, and elevated ESR and CRP, but not typically focal leg weakness

rejected.label: Iliopsoas bursitis
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings are not consistent with iliopsoas bursitis, which typically presents with hip pain and swelling, and imaging shows a fluid collection in the iliopsoas bursa

rejected.label: Giant cell arteritis
rejected.why: The patient's age and symptoms do not meet the typical criteria for giant cell arteritis, which includes headache, jaw claudication, and visual symptoms, and is typically seen in older adults with elevated ESR and CRP
